findings: ETT.tex:1940-1941: the middle step 'M -> A cap B is a Cauchy embedding, so phi(Sigma) is a Cauchy surface of A cap B' is not needed for the conclusion; the last sentence (every point of A cap B on an inextensible causal curve of A cap B meeting phi(Sigma)) holds directly, and with phi(M) connected and contained in A cap B it gives connectedness from M connected alone, without Geroch's splitting / a connected Cauchy surface.

Of the middle step, the uniqueness half is proved (every causal curve of every open set of N meets phi(Sigma) at most once, given CurvesExtend); the existence half (every inextensible curve of A cap B meets phi(Sigma)) stays unproved in the abstract setting: CurvesExtend extends segments only, and an inextensible curve of A cap B over an open interval would need to lie, with a reparametrisation, on an inextensible curve of N.

Hypotheses of SubExtension.c_ext_connexe that are not the paper's are not used here: N causally arc-connected, hthrough, and the sorry'd exists_mem_image_inf ('phi(Sigma) is a Cauchy surface of A cap B', an intermediate step of the paper's proof, not a hypothesis). The generic core needs only: T Cauchy in A and in B, and T meeting every inextensible curve of N at most once (Cauchy in N, or acausal in N).

CBG-DESIGN.md §3 step 3 'a Cauchy inclusion into a causal T2 spacetime with CurvesExtend is causally convex' is false as stated for non-absolutely-minimal (non-local) causalities: the gated line (timelike line plus an isolated point *, with a <= * for a <= 10 in every open set containing a, * and the gate 5) is causal, T2, globally hyperbolic with a continuous time function (so CurvesExtend), A = ]-1,1[ u {*} is Cauchy-included in it with the common Cauchy surface {g 0, *}, and A is not causally convex (g 0 <= 5 <= *, 5 notin A); the gated line is not absolutely minimal (conjunct of the witness theorem; gateLine_not_absolutelyMinimalOn). Under Level A (absolutely minimal on every open), the setting the design's claim concerns, whether arc-connectedness can be dropped is OPEN. The repair carried here is causal arc-connectedness of the ambient set, which flat instances have.

isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup (the union has S as a Cauchy surface) needs no arc-connectedness: uniqueness puts the segment of the curve between two parameters meeting S on an inextensible curve of B (CurvesExtendOn B) — Sbierski's 'gamma is also a segment of an inextendible curve in M'. Arc-connectedness is used only for convexity, hence GH of the union.

Non-trivial joint witness: timelikeLine_causalConvex_proper (A = ]-1,1[ a proper open subset of B = ℝ on the timelike line: Cauchy inclusion, B arc-connected with curves extending, A causally convex, union of {A, B} a Cauchy inclusion of A).
questions: Can absolute minimality of the causality (Level A's standing assumption) replace causal arc-connectedness in step 1? The witness does not settle it.

kb_proposals: An open set U seen as a spacetime without a subtype: C.relativeTo U := (C.restrict U).extend (Causal/Local.lean). Inextensible U for C is Inextensible ⊤ for C.relativeTo U (relativeTo_inextensible_top), and inextensibility in W <= U reads only the relations below W (inextensible_congr_causality); so every ⊤-only curve lemma (e.g. inextensible_ordConnectedComponent) gets its relative form in ~5 lines (inextensible_ordConnectedComponent_of_le), needing only <=_U antisymmetric.

Do not read Cauchy surfaces of C.relativeTo U on ⊤: constant curves at points outside U are inextensible there and meet nothing; transfer curve statements, not IsCauchySurface, and reprove the relative Cauchy lemma (IsCauchySurfaceOn.of_le) with the relative component lemma.

Causal convexity of a Cauchy inclusion is proved with causal arc-connectedness of the ambient open set (to realise <=_B by a curve) besides T2 and CurvesExtendOn; GH of the inclusion is not used. The Cauchy property of a union of Cauchy inclusions needs only CurvesExtendOn of the ambient set (segments of a curve lie on inextensible curves of B), not arc-connectedness.

lem:C_ext_connexe needs no connected Cauchy surface: phi(M) is connected and inside A cap B, and every point of A cap B is joined to phi(Sigma) inside A cap B (inf_component_meets); use c_ext_connexe_of_connectedSpace, whose hypotheses are the paper's (M connected) plus N T2 and CurvesExtend.

Convexity is false without causal arc-connectedness for non-absolutely-minimal (non-local) causalities (gated line witness, which is not absolutely minimal; kb/0019 scope); open under Level A. A causality whose relations are not realised by curves (nor by chains of localised relations) can add relations that Cauchy surfaces, defined through curves, do not see. Carry CausallyArcConnectedOn B (flat instances have it).

Abstract counterexamples on a disjoint union ℝ ⊕ Unit are cheap: inl ∘ g (g strictly monotone, continuous, open) is an IsEMorphism from timelikeLine, so isCauchySurfaceOn_image_iff transports {s} Cauchy; causal curves stay in one summand (Sum.isLeft continuous into discrete Bool on each segment).
